[ChroMenu Search] Notify once per query change in the search bar

Once an IME composition survives row changes (crrev.com/c/8812724), each
composition update or commit while search results are showing made the
menu jump to its full height for a frame on Linux.

The search bar used the Textfield's text changed callback, which also
fires for the intermediate state of an edit: replacing or committing a
composition first removes it, which looks like a cleared query, then
inserts the new text. The search controller restored the full menu and
showed the results again on every composition update or commit.

The search bar now notifies once per change of the query, with the final
text: via ContentsChanged() for user edits,
AppMenuSearchBarView::SetText() for programmatic ones, and
HandleAccessibleAction() for kSetValue. An edit that leaves the text
unchanged does not notify.

stored message with the new ScriptMessageValue class.

Let F6/Alt+Shift+A focus the inactive permission prompt

BrowserFocusControllerViews::ActivateFirstInactiveBubbleForAccessibility
only looked for bubbles anchored to a fixed set of anchors. The
permission prompt is anchored to the permission chip, so once it lost
focus (e.g. after clicking into the page), F6 and the focus-inactive-
popup accelerator could not bring focus back to it. This affected both
the Views and the WebUI location bar.

Look up the request and indicator chips through BrowserElements. Both
location bars register their chips under the same element identifiers,
and BubbleDialogDelegate::GetAnchoredDialog() already resolves bubbles
anchored to WebUI TrackedElements.

The one-time permission prompt has neither an initially focused view nor
a cancel button, since its buttons aren't dialog buttons, so the bubble
was found but nothing got focus. Fall back to
BubbleDialogDelegate::FocusFromAnchor(), which focuses the first
focusable view and activates the bubble, the same as Tab from the
anchor.

[Android/A11y] Dedupe AccessibilityTabHelper WebContents state init

TabImpl.initWebContents triggers both TabHelpers.initWebContentsHelpers
and notifyContentChanged, causing AccessibilityTabHelper (a TabObserver
registered once on the Tab) to invoke
updateWebContentsAccessibilityState() on WebContentsAccessibility
multiple times for the same WebContents during tab initialization and
restoration.

Extend TabWebContentsUserData so accessibility state updates run at most
once per WebContents swap, and skip redundant updates on window detach
while still refreshing when attached to a new activity window.

[Android] Observe all of a profile's tab models in AutoFetchPageLoadWatcher

AutoFetchPageLoadWatcher's TabWatcher observes only the first regular
tab model of its profile, assuming there is at most one. With multiple
windows, a profile has one tab model per window, so closing a request's
tab in any other window was missed, and the in-progress notification
was not shown for that request.

Observe every regular tab model of the profile, including models added
later, e.g. for a new window, and stop observing a model when it is
removed.

Match multi-word queries across titles and synonyms in menu search

Typing a multi-word query like "delete cache", "dark mode", or "window
incognito" in menu or settings search currently returns nothing when the
words live in different fields (such as title and synonym, or separate
synonyms) or appear out of order. Meanwhile, queries with an unrelated
second word like "delete banana" can still slip through via typo
tolerance.

Score multi-word queries word-by-word in addition to scoring the whole
phrase, requiring every word to match at least one field above the
minimum threshold and at least one word to meet the minimum query
length:
- Combines matches across the title, secondary text, and synonyms, and
  merges all matched title ranges.
- Discounts split-word scores so an exact in-order phrase match ranks
  above a split or cross-field match.
- Rejects queries where any word fails to match (such as "delete
  banana" or "delete x") or where every word is a single character (such
  as "a b").

Also remove duplicate unit tests in fuzzy_finder_unittest.cc that were
already covered by the custom-weight, min-score, and max-results tests.

[block-model] Compute MediaCodec OutputFrame eligibility

OutputFrame probe (1/4): eligibility check.

MediaCodec block model can hand out each decoded frame as an
AHardwareBuffer (MediaCodec.OutputFrame). Before Chrome probes or uses
that, it has to know which decoders are eligible:

- Block model in use: getOutputFrame() requires block-model mode;
  ShouldUseBlockModel() also gates on Android 17 26Q4+ and keeps
  MediaCrypto (including L3) off unless kMediaCodecBlockModelEncrypted
  is enabled.
- SurfaceControl on: OutputFrames reuse the SurfaceControl /
  GetAHardwareBuffer() path rather than legacy AndroidOverlay.
- Threaded texture mailboxes off: excludes WebView's mailbox path.
- Non-secure codec: hardware-secure (L1) protected buffers stay on the
  secure Surface path.
- Hardware codec: software codecs allocate CPU buffers that aren't
  GPU-sampleable.
- Surface is the TextureOwner: guards against external overlay Surfaces
  so GetAHardwareBuffer() and Surface fallback remain available.

MediaCodecVideoDecoder now decides this for each configured codec. When
block model is in use, it records the result, or the first blocker, to
Media.Android.MediaCodec.OutputFrame.Eligibility and logs it to
MediaLog.

kMediaCodecBlockModelOutput is checked last, and only for decoders that
pass the other checks, so only those clients are reported as part of
its field trial.

Nothing acts on the result yet. Follow-up CLs in this probe series add
the JNI getOutputFrame() bridge (2/4), CodecWrapper probing (3/4), and
decoder-side probe wiring (4/4); rendering remains on the Surface path
throughout.

[ozone/wayland] Keep compositor-set size on client-initiated resizes

A client-initiated resize (window.resizeTo() on a popup, or CDP
Browser.setWindowBounds) was applied to a toplevel in the xdg-shell
tiled state as if it were floating. Chromium then committed a window
geometry smaller than the configured size, while tiling compositors
such as Sway keep the tile at the configured size. The window was
drawn in the top-left corner of its tile with the rest unpainted, and
Chromium and the compositor disagreed about the window size until the
next configure.

The same path committed a shrunk geometry for maximized windows, e.g.
window.resizeTo() on a maximized popup or Document Picture-in-Picture
window, which violates the xdg-shell requirement to obey the
maximized size.

WaylandToplevelWindow::SetBoundsInDIP() now keeps the configured size
and only takes the requested origin when the window is maximized,
fullscreen, or has any tiled edge. This matches
OnStateRequestApplied(), which already treats any tiled edge as
compositor-sized. Keeping only some axes would not hold: Mutter
re-sends the half tile size on focus and suspend changes, and quarter
tiles have no axis with both edges tiled.

ash/input_method: use BCP-47 IDs in base::i18n::CreateTransliterator

Migrate `DiacriticsInsensitiveStringComparator` from
`base::i18n::CreateTransliteratorFromRules` to
`base::i18n::CreateTransliterator` using Chromium's pre-baked BCP-47-T
ID (`und-t-und-x0-diacstr`, backed by `CustomRulesForBcp47Id` on ICU4C
and pre-compiled `icu4x_data` on ICU4X).

The `und-t-und-x0-diacstr` rule set originates directly from the rules
previously inline in `DiacriticsInsensitiveStringComparator` with no
behavioral modifications.

This unblocks removing `CreateTransliteratorFromRules` and switching
`base::i18n::Transliterator` to ICU4X without compiling rules at
runtime.

[Wayland] Compose c with cedilla for Dead<acute>+c when GTK does

On Wayland, keys that the compositor IME doesn't consume go through
ui::CharacterComposer, whose table comes from the en_US Compose file
and maps Dead<acute> followed by c to U+0107 (c with acute). GTK apps
produce U+00E7 (c with cedilla) instead when the locale is pt_BR (GTK
loads the pt_BR Compose table) or when the "cedilla" input method is
selected with GTK_IM_MODULE/QT_IM_MODULE, which is the usual setup for
US International users who type Portuguese.

Add an option to CharacterComposer that maps Dead<acute>+c/C to ç/Ç,
and enable it from WaylandInputMethodContext when GTK_IM_MODULE or
QT_IM_MODULE selects "cedilla" first or the LC_CTYPE locale (LC_ALL,
LC_CTYPE, LANG) is pt_BR. The behavior is guarded by the
enabled-by-default kill switch WaylandCedillaCompose.

[AppMenu] Add zoom and fullscreen search synonyms

The zoom and full screen controls in the app menu are icon buttons
without text labels, so menu search falls back to their tooltips and
previously had no synonyms. As a result, queries such as "zoom in",
"zoom out", and "magnify" returned no results, and the zoom tooltips
appeared in Title Case unlike "Full screen".

- Add search synonyms for the zoom in, zoom out, and full screen actions
- Update the zoom tooltips to sentence case with matching translation
  screenshot
- Add browser test coverage for the new synonyms.

Screenshot: https://screenshot.corp.google.com/2d64ss865k260

Reland "[Sync] Pass Profile to PassphraseActivity via ProfileTokenUtils"

This is a reland of commit dea1008f9be9056f7a11e4c23f7ebcf8d1ad245d

It was reverted because two PassphraseActivityTest tests failed on
Android 10 (android-10-x86-rel): after recreateActivity(), the
deferred Profile resolution was never requested.

That was a test bug. The test helper started the activity with the
Profile token and then called ActivityTestUtils.waitForActivity(),
which starts a second instance with its own intent, without the token.
On Android 10 the test got that second instance back, so recreating it
took the no-token fallback, which doesn't resolve the Profile
asynchronously. On Android 15 it got the first instance back. The
helper now waits for the activity started by its own intent. The
test also now spies on the real ProfileResolver natives and only
defers resolveProfileFromBytes(). No production code changes.

Original change's description:
> [Sync] Pass Profile to PassphraseActivity via ProfileTokenUtils
>
> SyncErrorNotifier now attaches its Profile to the PassphraseActivity
> launch intent via ProfileTokenUtils.addProfileToIntent().
> PassphraseActivity now extends SynchronousInitializationActivity and
> gets its Profile in onProfileAvailable(), instead of calling
> ProfileManager.getLastUsedRegularProfile().
>
> Because the Profile may now resolve asynchronously (e.g. when it has to
> be loaded from disk), PassphraseActivity drops the dialogs restored by
> super.onCreate() if the Profile isn't available yet. The right dialog is
> shown again once it is. No dialog is shown if the Profile becomes
> available after the activity started finishing. Also fix
> isShowingDialog(), which looked in the platform FragmentManager instead
> of the support FragmentManager the dialogs are added to. Because of
> that, recreating the activity showed a second passphrase dialog on top
> of the restored one.
>
> SyncErrorNotifier's notification tag and PendingIntent identity are now
> per-Profile, using ProfileTokenUtils. With multiple Profiles, one
> Profile's sync error notification no longer replaces or clears another
> Profile's. Clearing the notification also uses the tag now; before,
> cancel() was called without the tag the notification was posted with, so
> a resolved error never cleared it. The notification posted under the
> old, shared tag is cancelled once, when the notifier is created, until
> that path is removed in M163.
>
> Bug: 40254448, 585922618

[mojo] Let feature params select the ipcz parcel capacity policy

Add a MojoIpczParcelCapacityPolicy feature whose "policy" param selects
one of ipcz's parcel capacity policies or its default dynamic growth.

ipcz only takes memory flags at node creation, so the policy is read in
InitFeatures(), which every content process calls with params before
Init(). Child processes get the browser's params, and DirectReceiver's
per-thread node copies the process node's memory flags, so an arm
applies one policy everywhere. When the feature is off or the param is
missing or unknown, and in embedders that don't call InitFeatures(), the
policy stays fixed.

The Mac app shim reads Mojo features through an early-access allowlist,
so the feature is listed there to avoid a CHECK.

[Clank Multiprofile] Gate post-native Activity init on ProfileProvider

This should prevent issues with the *WithNative lifecycle activities
from worrying whether a profile is loaded or not.

If we start a new activity (and native is already loaded), this CL will
simply block kicking off all the queued functions (including
startNativeInitialization, which is what will fire the *WithNative
lifecycle events) until profileProviderSupplier has resolved the profile
object.

local_search_service: use BCP-47 IDs in base::i18n::CreateTransliterator

Migrate `CreateDiacriticRemover` and `CreateHyphenRemover` from
`base::i18n::CreateTransliteratorFromRules` to
`base::i18n::CreateTransliterator` using Chromium's pre-baked BCP-47-T
IDs (`und-t-und-x0-dropacc` and `und-t-und-x0-rmhyph`, backed by
`CustomRulesForBcp47Id` on ICU4C and pre-compiled `icu4x_data` on
ICU4X).

This unblocks removing `CreateTransliteratorFromRules` and switching
`base::i18n::Transliterator` to ICU4X without compiling rules at
runtime.

[History] Use illustration color tokens for Android empty state

On Android, empty_state_illustration.html.ts used UI role tokens
(--color-sys-primary-container, --color-sys-primary, and
--color-sys-secondary). Activity theme overrides replace those UI
roles, and --color-sys-secondary resolves to Secondary40/Secondary80
instead of the Secondary60/Secondary70 illustration tones.

Switch to --color-sys-illo-primary-min, --color-sys-illo-primary-max,
and --color-sys-illo-secondary-high. Keep the cr_shared_vars.css
primary fallbacks before colors.css loads since it doesn't define a
secondary/illustration fallback. Non-Android builds are unchanged.

[Unified Tabstrip] Animate out children of closing views

Even with the previous fix in crrev.com/c/8822238, while closing all
tabs in a a group, one last tab in the group does not animate out
because the TabStripModel removes the entire group collection when there
is only one tab left, and doesn't send out the tab removal notification
for that.

This CL fixes things by performing deinitialization on collection nodes
that are closed. Deinitialize() is additionally refactored to iterate
over tab collection node children instead of the backing tab collection.

[Wayland] Draw tablet tool cursors without the cursor shape protocol

On compositors without wp_cursor_shape_manager_v1, such as GNOME 46
and 47, Chrome never set a cursor for a tablet tool after proximity_in,
so the stylus had no cursor at all over Chrome windows. Custom cursors
also fell back to the default shape on all compositors.

WaylandCursor now sets its surface as the cursor of a
WaylandCursor::Device, implemented by WaylandPointer with
wl_pointer.set_cursor and by WaylandTabletTool with
zwp_tablet_tool_v2.set_cursor. A tablet tool draws cursors that the
compositor has no shape for on a WaylandCursor of its own. Theme
cursors are shown without animation there, as the tool's cursor
doesn't take part in the theme lifetime tracking of the
WaylandCursorBufferListener.

[actor] [page stabilization] Defer and reuse delayers in ToolController

Adds the ToolController side of waiting for page stability once per
bundle of page actions (kActorStabilizeOncePerBundle):

- Invoke() takes an optional `deferred_observation_config`. When set,
  the tool's result isn't delayed until the page is ready for
  observation. Its ObservationDelayController is kept armed as a
  pending observation instead.
- The next tool reuses the pending delayer if it acts on the same
  document. The renderer-side PageStabilityMonitor was armed before the
  first deferred tool acted, so a single wait covers the changes made by
  every tool of the bundle. The wait uses the start delay of the tool
  that closes the bundle.
- ShouldSettlePendingObservationBefore() tells whether a request can't
  reuse the pending delayer (not a page tool on the same tab and
  document, or the page navigated), and SettlePendingObservation() waits
  on it without invoking another tool.
- A tool that reuses the delayer waits on it even if the tool fails,
  when a deferred tool requires waiting for the page.
- Cancel() drops the pending observation. A failure in
  CreateToolAndValidate() keeps it so the caller can still settle it.

Also adds ToolRequest::AsPageToolRequest() and Tool::GetTargetFrame().

Nothing passes `deferred_observation_config` yet, so there's no behavior
change.

[Wayland] Apply the window cursor to tablet tools

On Wayland, a tablet tool has a cursor of its own, separate from the
one of wl_pointer. WaylandTabletTool set it to the default shape on
proximity_in and never changed it, and WaylandWindow::UpdateCursorShape
only updated the cursor of wl_pointer. So CSS cursors, including
"cursor: none", had no effect on a stylus.

WaylandTabletTool now keeps the proximity_in serial and target window
until proximity_out. When a window's cursor is loaded, it is forwarded
to the tools in proximity of the window, independently of wl_pointer
focus, and a tool entering proximity takes on the window's current
cursor. A tool hides its cursor with zwp_tablet_tool_v2.set_cursor and
shows it with wp_cursor_shape_device_v1. Bitmap cursors aren't supported
for tablet tools yet, so custom cursors fall back to the default shape,
and compositors without wp_cursor_shape_manager_v1 keep their own
cursor.

The test Wayland server gets zwp_tablet_manager_v2 and
wp_cursor_shape_manager_v1 support for the new tests.

[MChips] Make the composeplate's trailing button configurable

This is a refactor CL without any behaviour changes.

The last button of the composeplate on the NTP is hard-wired to be the
incognito button: its icon, strings and metrics are fixed. The
merchandising chips experiment needs to show an image chip in that
position in some arms, so the button has to be configurable in the same
way as the optional button.

In this CL:
- Rename the incognito button to the trailing button: its view ids,
  property keys and the ComposeplateCoordinator API.
- Add property keys and ComposeplateCoordinator setters for the trailing
  button's icon, text and content description. The layout keeps the
  incognito icon and strings as its defaults.
- Pass the button type along with the trailing button's click listener,
  and record its click and impression metrics with that type instead of
  always as the incognito button.

The NTP still sets up the trailing button as the incognito button, so
there is no behavior change. A follow-up CL uses the new setters to show
an image chip on it.

Clean up net/websockets/websocket_extension{,_parser}.{h,cc}

- Replace `Consume`, `Lookahead`, and the `remaining_` save/restore in
  `ConsumeIfMatch` with `ConsumeSpacesThenConsumeIfMatch`: every path
  following a mismatch (`'='` -> `';'` -> `','` -> `remaining_.empty()`,
  and `'"'` -> `ConsumeToken`) already skips horizontal whitespace next,
  so restoring `remaining_` on mismatch had no behavioral effect and
  only rescanned whitespace (and required an extra `ConsumeSpaces()`
  call in `Parse()` before checking `remaining_.empty()`).
- Have `ConsumeRestOfQuotedToken` (formerly `ConsumeQuotedToken`) assume
  the opening `'"'` was already consumed by
  `ConsumeSpacesThenConsumeIfMatch('"')`, simplify its loop to return
  early on the closing `'"'`, and use `HttpUtil::IsLWS` in
  `ConsumeSpaces`.
- Emplace parsed extensions and parameters directly into the target
  `std::vector<WebSocketExtension>` / `WebSocketExtension` instead of
  overwriting dummy locals, return early in `Parse()` on failure instead
  of tracking `bool failed`, and return `std::optional` from
  `ConsumeToken` and `ConsumeRestOfQuotedToken`.
- Initialize `remaining_` in `WebSocketExtensionParser`'s constructor,
  remove its explicit destructor, and rvalue-qualify `Parse() &&`.
- Support move construction and move assignment on `WebSocketExtension`
  and `WebSocketExtension::Parameter`, accept `std::string` and
  `Parameter` by value in their constructors and `Add()`, default
  `Parameter`'s `operator==`, and remove the unused default
  `WebSocketExtension` constructor.
- Change `ParseWebSocketExtensions` from `NET_EXPORT` to
  `NET_EXPORT_PRIVATE` to match `WebSocketExtension`, and fix IWYU in
  `websocket_extension.{h,cc}` and `websocket_extension_parser.cc`.

This change contains no intentional observable behavioral differences.

- `und-t-und-x0-dropacc`: Spoof-check / Ash local search diacritics
- `und-t-und-x0-xconf`: Spoof-check supplemental confusable mapping
- `und-t-und-x0-rmhyph`: Ash local search hyphen/dash removal
- `und-t-und-x0-diacstr`: Ash input method Western European diacritics

In the legacy `!BUILDFLAG(BUILD_RUST_TRANSLIT)` ICU4C branch, map these
IDs via `CustomRulesForBcp47Id` in `//base/i18n/transliterator.cc` while
keeping `CreateTransliteratorFromRules` temporarily until per-component
follow-up CLs migrate all callers and remove it. Also add unit tests
covering all 6 custom IDs and sync `extra_conf.txt` and
`common/transliterator_rules_v1.rs.data` with https://crrev.com/c/8832798
(mapping U+045F `џ` to `u`).

[Menus] Confirm a menu Textfield's IME composition when it loses focus

When a menu takes focus away from a Textfield it hosts, the platform
ends the IME session but the Textfield keeps its composition. If focus
then returns by keyboard, the menu still leaves keys to the IME, so
Backspace does nothing and typing replaces the composed text.
crrev.com/c/8812724 stopped row rebuilds from blurring the field; this
covers the remaining case, such as hovering another row. Repro steps and
a before/after video are on the bug.

Confirm the composition in ClearFocusedTextfield() before clearing
focus. Confirming runs TextfieldController callbacks, so the function
holds a deletion guard and re-reads the focused Textfield afterwards.
Blurs that do not go through ClearFocusedTextfield(), such as hiding the
Textfield, are left for a follow-up in Textfield::OnBlur().

[Android/Tabs] Convert TrustedCdn to stateless utility

TrustedCdn was maintained as a stateful helper attached to every tab
even when unused or unnecessary.

Convert TrustedCdn to a stateless utility class to avoid unnecessary
object allocation and state tracking per tab.

[glic] Add chrome://flags entry for Glic Activity Hub

Glic's unified Activity Hub for tracking asynchronous activities is
gated behind features::kGlicActivityHub, which is disabled by default.
Without a chrome://flags entry, testing or dogfooding Activity Hub
requires passing --enable-features=GlicActivityHub on the command line.

This CL exposes the "glic-activity-hub" flag in chrome://flags across
Desktop and Android, along with its flag descriptions, expiry metadata,
and LoginCustomFlags histogram enum entries.

[Unified tabstrip] Don't animate layout when widget is not visible

Skip tab strip layout animations in TabStripCollectionController when
the widget is missing or invisible, matching legacy TabContainer.

Previously, adding a tab before the window was shown started an
animation at 0.0, keeping TabStripView empty and preventing
features::kDeferLayoutDuringBrowserStartup from deferring subsequent
layouts, which broke BrowserViewDeferLayoutTest.

Fix GWP-ASan and on-demand heap profiling in release/official builds

https://crrev.com/c/8626429 used
`EXPENSIVE_TEST_LOGIC_IS_ON()` to guard these. However,
`EXPENSIVE_TEST_LOGIC_IS_ON()` is enable_expensive_dchecks = false
in all non-DCHECK release builds and official builds, not only test
binaries.

Using it directly in `ChromeMainDelegate::InitializeMemorySystem()`
disabled GWP-ASan in production release/official builds and switched
`PoissonAllocationSamplerInclusion` to `kDynamic`, breaking on-demand
Perfetto trace (`org.chromium.sampling_heap_profiler` /
`HeapProfilingDataSource`) and DevTools (`Memory.startSampling`) heap
profiling whenever `HeapProfilerController` was not already active at
startup.

To fix this while preserving the fast-test GWP-ASan skip:
1. Restore `PoissonAllocationSamplerInclusion::kEnforce` unconditionally
   in `ChromeMainDelegate` and `ShellMainDelegate`. Since
   https://crrev.com/c/8657621 already defers connecting `Dispatcher`
   allocation hooks until `PoissonAllocationSampler` starts, `kEnforce`
   incurs zero hook overhead when heap profiling is inactive.
2. Check `!command_line->HasSwitch(switches::kTestType)` alongside
   `EXPENSIVE_TEST_LOGIC_IS_ON()` for `SetGwpAsanParameters()` so
   GWP-ASan is only skipped in fast test runs (`--test-type`) and not in
   production builds.

[gpu] Enforce usages in ProduceDawnBuffer

ProduceDawnBuffer has only 1 production callsite from WebNN which
uses it with WebGPU interop. Thus ProduceDawnBuffer should be called
with WEBGPU_READ | WEBGPU_WRITE | WEBGPU_SHARED_BUFFER usages at
the least. Also update ClientSharedImage::BeginWebGPUBufferAccess
to also check for these usages and put behind killswitch enabled
by default. Also update unittests that try ProduceDawnBuffer on
SI with incorrect usages to skip when `use_shared_buffer_` is not set
(metal).

activity_reporter: Report every requested app as active

ActivityService returned only kChromeActivityId as active, whatever ids
update_client passed to GetActiveBits() and GetAndClearActiveBits().

own app id (crrev.com/c/8817646).

arc: Notify Sync when ARC app connection closes

ArcPackageSyncDataTypeController previously gated GetPreconditionState()
on ArcAppListPrefs::package_list_initial_refreshed() without overriding
OnAppConnectionClosed(). When OnConnectionClosed() reset
package_list_initial_refreshed_ to false, Sync was not notified to stop
ARC_PACKAGE, so an in-flight initial update could hit the DCHECK in
MergeDataAndStartSyncing(). OnConnectionClosed() also called
StopSyncing() directly, desynchronizing ArcPackageSyncableService from
SyncableServiceBasedBridge across KEEP_METADATA pauses.

Override OnAppConnectionClosed() to call
DataTypePreconditionChanged(ARC_PACKAGE), let SyncableServiceBasedBridge
own StopSyncing(), and add unit tests covering disconnect and reconnect.

Bug: b:586598231

[MChips] Rename the gallery chip to add image and split its metrics enum

This is a refactoring CL without any behaviour changes.
Spec: http://shortn/_QWUHUh5Yv2.

The composeplate's add image chip is still called "gallery" in
ActionChips and ModuleTypeOnStartAndNtp, while the UI and the feature
flag call it "add image". ActionChips is also both the action_chips
feature param and the enum of the
NewTabPage.Composeplate.Buttons.Impression histogram, which stops
working once the param gets a value for a combination of chips, which
isn't a button.

In this CL:
- Rename ActionChips.GALLERY to ADD_IMAGE and
  ModuleTypeOnStartAndNtp.COMPOSEPLATE_VIEW_GALLERY_BUTTON to
  COMPOSEPLATE_VIEW_ADD_IMAGE_BUTTON, and update the enum labels in
  enums.xml.
- Add ComposeplateMetricsUtils.ComposeplateViewButtonType, a per-button
  enum that keeps the recorded values, and record the button impressions
  and the optional button's type with it. ActionChips is now only the
  feature param.
- Rename the histogram enum from NtpActionChips to
  NtpComposeplateViewButtonType to match.
- Add ActionChips.ADD_IMAGE_AND_CREATE_IMAGE, the param value for
  showing both image chips, which has no ComposeplateViewButtonType
  counterpart. A follow-up CL shows the two chips.

The recorded values don't change. The only behavior change is for
action_chips=4, which no config uses yet: clicking the AI Mode button
now redirects to the AI Mode omnibox, like the other non-default values.
The buttons shown don't change.

The omnibox-owned names for this chip,
OmniboxFocusReason.NTP_GALLERY_CHIP_CLICKED and
AiModeActivationSource.NTP_GALLERY_BUTTON, are not renamed here.

[Actor] Allow background activity start in notification restart test

Currently, sending the notification PendingIntent after finishing the
activity is blocked on Android 14+ by background activity launch
restrictions, causing the restart test from crrev.com/c/8804315 to fail
and leading crrev.com/c/8827442 to disable it on Android 14.

configure ActivityOptions with ApiCompatibilityUtils'
setActivityOptionsBackgroundActivityStartAllowAlways, pass the bundle to
PendingIntent.send, and remove the @DisableIf.Build suppression.

[Android] Make AutoFetchNotifier per-profile

Pass the Profile of OfflinePageAutoFetcherService to AutoFetchNotifier
when showing or updating the in-progress notification and when showing
the complete notification, which now gets the offline page's
LoadUrlParams from that Profile instead of
ProfileManager.getLastUsedRegularProfile().

Scope the in-progress notification to that Profile, so that profiles no
longer overwrite each other's notification or cancel each other's
requests:
- Tag the notification with ProfileTokenUtils.getNotificationTag().
- Attach the profile token to its cancel and delete intents, and give
  them a per-profile identity via
  ProfileTokenUtils.setProfileScopedIdentity().
- InProgressCancelReceiver closes the notification of the intent's
  Profile, and once the full browser is started, cancels the requests of
  that Profile.

Notifications posted before this change use the unscoped tag and have no
profile token. Until they expire:
- A tokenless cancel intent cancels the requests of the last used
  regular Profile, and closes the unscoped notification.
- When the request count of the initial profile, the only one that could
  have posted such a notification, reaches 0, its unscoped notification
  is closed too.

The cancellation pref, which records a cancellation made while Chrome
isn't running, stays app-wide, so only the initial profile consumes it
on startup.

Follow-ups:
- crbug.com/587417706: Honor cancellations of non-initial profiles made
  while Chrome isn't running, via per-profile SharedPreferences.
- crbug.com/587416933: Replace the global "showing in-progress" pref.
- crbug.com/587418020: Give the cancel and delete PendingIntents
  distinct request codes.

Fix macOS status tray icon keyboard and screen reader accessibility

Fixes keyboard and screen-reader accessibility for OS status tray icons
(such as the Gemini in Chrome OS entry point) on macOS:

- Previously, when open_menu_with_secondary_click_ was enabled,
  StatusIconMac left item_.menu nil so left-clicks would invoke
  handleClick: instead of opening the menu, and handleClick: ignored any
  activation where NSApp.currentEvent.type != NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown.
  This broke both VoiceOver Ctrl+Option+Space (AXPress arrives via Mach
  IPC without a mouse NSEvent) and macOS Fn+Ctrl+F8 ("Move focus to
  status menus", where -[NSStatusItem _participatesInNavigationLoop]
  requires item.menu != nil). Setting only button.toolTip also populated
  AXHelp without AXDescription.
- Keep item().menu populated and observed across all StatusIconMac
  modes, and swizzle -[NSStatusBarButton mouseDown:] alongside
  rightMouseDown: so plain left-clicks (without Control) dispatch
  DispatchClickEvent() directly when open_menu_with_secondary_click() is
  true while Control-clicks, right-clicks, VoiceOver AXPress, and
  Fn+Ctrl+F8 open item.menu.
- Defer rebuilding menu_ if a model update arrives while the menu is
  actively tracking (posting FlushDeferredMenuRebuild() after
  NSMenuDidEndTrackingNotification so NSMenuItem's weak target stays
  alive through itemSelected: action dispatch).
- Populate button.accessibilityLabel alongside button.toolTip in
  SetToolTip() so VoiceOver announces AXDescription immediately, clear
  observation_ and item_.menu when SetContextMenu(nullptr) is called,
  and set force_show_accelerator_for_item before updating the
  accelerator in GlicStatusIcon::UpdateHotkey() so eager NSMenu builds
  include the shortcut keyEquivalent.

Bug: b:526650564
Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter="StatusIconMacTest.*:GlicStatusIconTest.*"

🛡 [Omnibox] Drop unedited page-derived input on tab switch restore

An input session retained across tab switches is restored as-is when
its tab is selected again, on the assumption that the retained text is
the user's own and therefore independent of the page. That assumption
does not hold for the initial text: on devices with the desktop
experience it is derived from the URL of the page the session was
started on, and it is only refreshed on the first activation. If the
tab shows a different page by the time it is selected again, the
restored text describes a page that is no longer there.

Add FuseboxSessionState.isInitialInputForOtherPage(), which reports an
active session whose user text is still the initial text and whose
initial text was derived from a page other than the current one, and
make LocationBarMediator.onTabChanged() end such a session instead of
restoring it. The following onUrlChanged() then presents the current
page as it does for any tab without a session.

Text edited by the user is still restored unconditionally, sessions
are not ended by navigations of the active tab, and no new state is
kept: the URL the initial text was derived from is already retained as
the initial preview match URL.

media/gpu: Let AV1 accelerators decode spatial layers

Add AV1Accelerator::SupportsSpatialLayers(), false by default.
AV1Decoder rejects AV1 streams with spatial layers only when it is
false, so nothing changes for existing accelerators.

When it is true, AV1Decoder submits every frame of a temporal unit but
holds the last shown picture and outputs it once the DecoderBuffer is
fully decoded: the highest spatial layer actually received, which can
be below the operating point's top layer when an SFU drops layers.
Neither the RTP wildcard operating point nor an operating_point_idc of
0 says whether a stream has spatial layers, and side data may be
absent, so it always holds; a single-layer temporal unit has only one
shown frame (Spec 7.5). A temporal unit whose OBUs go down in
spatial_id, or that has two shown frames in one spatial layer, is
rejected as malformed (Spec 7.5).

[UndoTabClosures] Support restoring archived tabs for undo

Plumbs the backend restoration path so archived tabs saved to
TabRestoreService can be restored directly into ArchivedTabModel as
frozen tabs without allocating a live WebContents:

- Rename ClosureKind.SAVED_GROUPS, forSavedGroups, captureSavedGroups,
  and getSavedGroupsContent to ARCHIVED / forArchived (accepting a
  TabRestoreEntryId) / captureArchived / getArchivedContent.
- Add WebContentsState::CreateContentsStateAsByteBuffer and
  TabModel::CreateFrozenTab so AndroidLiveTabContextUndoRestoreWrapper
  restores TabModelType::kArchived entries directly into frozen tabs via
  TabModelJniBridge#createFrozenTab and
  ArchivedTabCreator#createFrozenTab (with
  TabLaunchType.FROM_UNDO_CLOSURE and dirty TabStateAttributes) without
  creating a throwaway WebContents.
- Share RecentlyClosedBridge ownership and restoreForUndo in
  TabModelSelectorBase so ArchivedTabModelSelectorImpl can restore from
  TabRestoreService, and enable archived-model restoration in
  TabCollectionTabModelImpl#restoreClosedTabsForUndo while skipping
  group and selection restoration.

73098e224c9522e3cd0d6552f85c5dce234cb653 [ diff ] 
media: Use `AOM_Q` with bounded QP range for AV1 in CQP mode

Previously `Av1VideoEncoder` configured `Bitrate::Mode::kExternal` using
`AOM_CBR` and per-frame `AV1E_SET_QUANTIZER_ONE_PASS`. This comes with a
number of issues for quality, e.g. cyclic refresh and some loop-filter
related things aren't possible.

This CL changes the mode to `AOM_Q` instead, and limits min/max QP to be
within a small distance of what `encode_options.quantizer` asks for and
set the target QP via `AOME_SET_CQ_LEVEL`.

A quantizer of 0 is still clamped to exactly 0, so it stays in lossless
encoding mode without any QP variability.

While this technically diverges from a true CQP mode, given that the
target QP is still correct on average and the allowed delta is small,
this should not pose any problems in practice.

[downloads] List downloads in progress in the download tray

The full download tray, opened from the toolbar download button, now
lists downloads in progress above the recent ended ones, as desktop's
download bubble does: running and pending downloads first, then paused
ones, each most recently started first, under one cap of 30 rows.

A row shows a progress bar and a status line such as
"65.00 MB / 100.00 MB • 15 secs left", "… • Paused" or "… • Pending",
and follows its download while the tray is open: it updates as the
download progresses, and stays in place when it ends or is retried.
Rows are display only for now; only a completed row opens its file.

All rows share one layout, so the RowType IntDef is replaced by a
single view type.

media: Update av1-svc-L2T2.ivf to libaom's re-levelled vector

av1-svc-L2T2.ivf was libaom's av1-1-b8-22-svc-L2T2.ivf, whose sequence
header declares level 2.1 for its 1280x720 top layer, so libgav1's
level check rejects it. libaom replaced it with
av1-1-b8-22-svc-L2T2-2.ivf (aom 293d257), which differs only in
declaring level 3.1. Use that one, so that tests of spatial-layer
decoding can use this vector.

The existing tests only check that AV1 streams with spatial layers are
rejected, and still pass.

The image extractor now returns, with each image, whether it came from

[ios] Add knowledge base rules: documentation-derived (1/2)

This CL is part of a chain that lands the iOS code review knowledge base
under //ios/agents/knowledge_base: Markdown rules that an automated
reviewer evaluates against the added lines of a CL. The philosophy is to
review them, but to err on the side of landing them as reasonably fast
as possible so we can get early feedback on the code review agent's
quality and iterate on individual rules as we go.

The knowledge base is import-only: this chain does not opt //ios into
automated review. A directory that is already opted in (agentic_review
in its DIR_METADATA) gets the rules by adding mixins:
"//ios/agents/knowledge_base/COMMON_METADATA" next to that block.

Rules derived directly from //ios/best_practices.md and
//ios/architecture/ (first half).

Rules in this CL:

- ios/all-ios-source-files-must-be-objective-cpp (general, should_fix, 1
  supporting CLs)
- ios/app-configuration-for-egtest-feature-flags (general, should_fix, 4
  supporting CLs)

  43 supporting CLs)

  should_fix, 0 supporting CLs)

[Editing] Fix a malformed expectation in a typing-around-link WPT

The "Replacing text in a link in <b>" subtest of
typing-around-link-element-at-collapsed-selection.tentative.html

variants. Expect "<b><a>XY</a></b>" instead.

[code-health] WebUI: Use ariaNotify() in CrA11yAnnouncer when available.

CrA11yAnnouncer announces messages by rewriting the contents of a
visually hidden live region. Live regions are unreliable: some screen
readers (e.g. Orca on Linux) frequently miss updates, and consecutive
identical messages are often not re-announced because the region's
content does not observably change.

Element.ariaNotify() posts announcements directly to the accessibility
tree and avoids these issues. It is enabled via the Blink AriaNotify
runtime feature on Android, Windows, Mac and Linux, but not yet on
ChromeOS, so feature-detect it at announcement time and keep the live
region as a fallback.

Messages are still batched by the existing timeout and the
cr-a11y-announcer-messages-sent event is still dispatched with the
same payload, so callers and tests listening for it are unaffected.
The notification is posted on the #messages element, whose explicit
role guarantees an accessibility object; Blink drops notifications
posted on nodes without one.

Update the unit tests to cover both the ariaNotify() path (including
consecutive identical messages) and the live region fallback, stubbing
ariaNotify() so that they behave the same on every platform.

b59b20db09588650ea847910fe8e685b028aad26 [ diff ] 
devtools: support av1 video_screenshot trace recording

Encode compositor frames from DevToolsVideoConsumer into AV1 chunks via
DevToolsMediaEncodingService in a sandboxed utility process and emit
Screenshot instant events under the
disabled-by-default-devtools.video_screenshot trace category.

Why containerless AV1 chunks (output: kEncodedFrames) instead of MP4 (output: kMp4)?
1) Each Screenshot trace event carries per-frame compositor metadata
   (frame_sequence, source_id, expected_display_time) to correlate with
   AnimationFrame events, whereas Mp4Muxer batches frames into 1s blobs.
2) Trace capture only records actual compositor updates and skips
   MediaRecorder's 1s idle frame keep-alive timer.
3) DevTools Frontend (https://crrev.com/c/8617073) feeds each event's
   av1_chunk directly into WebCodecs VideoDecoder without needing an MP4
   demuxer in the trace worker.

Notes:
- Page.startScreenRecording MP4 output now also uses
  media::VideoEncoder::ContentHint::Screen (enabling AOM_CONTENT_SCREEN
  tuning and palette mode).
- disabled-by-default-devtools.video_screenshot requires enable_libaom=true
  (no-op on 32-bit Android and CastOS where enable_libaom=false).

Design doc: https://goto.google.com/chrome-devtools:trace-video-screenshots-design

Fail GL access in ExternalVkImageBacking

If ExternalVkImageBacking is created to hold a NativePixmap, which only
happens on Fuchsia, don't allow ProduceGL() to return a GL texture.
ANGLE doesn't have enough information to import the pixmap to GL
correctly.

The GL texture is already broken when there is a pixmap so no legitimate
clients are using that. Malicious clients could request it so remove the
ability. Also move the GpuMemoryBufferHandle to NativePixmap conversion
earlier so that the create call fails when NativePixmap creation fails.

ExternalVkImageBacking is allowed to be created with USAGE_GLES2 and
buffer handle on Fuchsia but ideally we would change clients not to
include USAGE_GLES2 and reject it at the factory level as well.

ios: Use XCUIHinge and XCUIDevice on iPhone Duo simulator

Xcode 27.3 and the iOS 27.3 simulator runtime add XCUIDevice.hinge
(XCUIHinge.angle) and fix XCUIDevice.orientation on iPhone Duo.

Drive hinge angle and device orientation via XCUIDevice.hinge.angle
and XCUIDevice.orientation when running under Xcode 27.3+ on iOS
27.3+, falling back to the legacy IOKit virtual HID service on older
Xcode or simulator runtimes. Forward-declare the hinge property when
building against older Xcode SDKs so binaries built with Xcode 27.0
or 27.2 still use the public API when executed on 27.3. Keep in-app
UIHingeInteraction and window geometry checks since XCUIHinge.angle
returns before the display transition settles.

cc: Avoid color conversion when decoding gain maps

The RGB decode cache gives gain maps the base image's color space.
This can change their numeric samples before they reach the gain-map
shader, producing incorrect SDR tones with HDR-base JXL images.

Decode gain maps without a color space while keeping existing
base-image color handling. Add a regression for linear and PQ Rec.2020
bases, raw gain samples, and the base image's decode color space.

The regression fails before the fix in a matched older Chromium build.
Current-main compilation and a patched-browser display check are still
pending.

Bug: 476652050
Test: Historical cache suite: 496 passed, 2 expected skips.

Revert "[X11] Let the window manager move windows during tab dragging"

This reverts commit 6e5ee2c357125163c957405967d425394257d0fb.

Reason for revert: After detaching a tab with the window manager move
loop, aura::Env keeps the left mouse button marked as pressed because
the window manager consumes the button release. Tooltips are then
suppressed in all windows until the next click.

Original change's description:
> [X11] Let the window manager move windows during tab dragging
>
> When a tab is dragged out of a window on X11, Chrome moves the dragged
> window itself with ConfigureRequests. Mutter (GNOME) and Muffin
> (Cinnamon) treat those as client-initiated moves and keep the window
> fully inside the work area, so a large dragged window gets stuck at the
> screen edge and can't be brought to a tab strip below it.
>
> Moves that the window manager performs in response to
> _NET_WM_MOVERESIZE count as user actions and aren't constrained, which
> is also how dragging by the title bar already works. Use them for the
> tab-dragging move loop on the window managers the 2016 attempt
> (https://crrev.com/2410773002) allowlisted: Compiz, Metacity, Muffin and
> Mutter. Chrome keeps following the drag through the window's
> ConfigureNotify events. Since the window manager holds the pointer grab,
> the end of the drag is detected with XInput2 raw button release events
> on the root window, and ending the loop early (attaching the tabs to
> another tab strip) sends _NET_WM_MOVERESIZE_CANCEL. Newly created
> windows start the move once they are mapped, because window managers
> ignore the request for windows they don't manage yet. The move is
> anchored at the grabbed point of the window, so the window snaps under
> the pointer even if its initial position was constrained.
>
> The 2016 change was reverted for crbug.com/661248, a click on the custom
> title bar starting a move. That came from its title bar event handling,
> which this change doesn't touch.
>
> kX11WmMoveLoop is a kill switch.
>
> Tested on Xvfb + Mutter 47.3 --x11: a tab dragged out of a 1500x900
> window on a 1600x1000 screen now follows the pointer partly offscreen
> (window y=661 vs. stuck at y=125 with the feature disabled). Also
> checked reattaching to another tab strip mid-drag, detaching again in
> the same gesture, Escape, a quick release and later clicks.
>
> Fixed: 369158266
> Change-Id: I7f752ff11cfa8ee06db11f2c6eae6b28886454f7
> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8752566
> Commit-Queue: Thomas Anderson <thomasanderson@chromium.org>
> Reviewed-by: Nick Yamane <nickdiego@igalia.com>

Original change's description:
> [GEiC] Restrict raw Glic provider access with PassKeys
>
> Glic code branched on the latched `GlicProvider` instead of asking
> `GlicProviderSpec`, which spreads provider checks around the codebase.
>
> * Only provider-change detection and chrome://glic-internals can
>   identify the provider, through `PassKey`s; everything else uses
>   `GlicProviderSpec` capabilities.
> * Drop the leftover provider check in the Gemini Enterprise FRE helpers
>   (crbug.com/574495404); only the Gemini Enterprise FRE store calls
>   them.
> * Tests read the provider through `...ForTesting()` methods that only
>   run in tests.
>

media/gpu/mac: Optionally serialize VideoToolbox decodes

Add VideoToolboxDecompressionSessionMetadata::serialize_decodes. When
it is set, VideoToolboxDecompressionSessionManager submits a sample
only once every earlier decode has been output, so at most one decode
is in flight; OnOutput() resumes processing.

With several AV1 spatial-layer temporal units in flight, asynchronous
VideoToolbox decoding has been seen to output the base layer instead of
the top one. Nothing sets the flag yet; a later change sets it for AV1
sequences with spatial layers.

Bug: 573939397
Test: media_unittests
      --gtest_filter=VideoToolboxDecompressionSessionManagerTest.*

[Toolbar] Set up top padding before NTP test check

In `ToolbarPositionControllerTest`, the NTP early-return check ran
before an active tab or top padding was set. Without top padding to
clear, no capture would run anyway, so the assertion always passed.

We now set up the active tab and top padding before the NTP check. The
padding stays applied for the move to the bottom right after.

[symphonia] Number SymphoniaDemuxer tracks like FFmpegDemuxer

SymphoniaDemuxer uses Symphonia's container track IDs, such as Ogg
stream serial numbers, as MediaTrack IDs. FFmpegDemuxer numbers tracks
sequentially from 1, so the two demuxers report different track IDs to
the page for the same file.

Number tracks from 1 in the order they are added, and give each
SymphoniaDemuxerStream its MediaTrack ID instead of deriving it from
the Symphonia track ID. Track labels still need Symphonia to expose
track names.

[media] Cycle threads before checking external memory in WMPI tests

In WebMediaPlayerImplTest.LoadPreloadMetadataSuspendNoVideoMemoryUsage
(and sibling preload=metadata suspend tests), OnPipelineSuspended()
calls ReportMemoryUsage(), which posts RespondToDemuxerMemoryUsageReport
to media_thread_ and then FinishMemoryUsageReport back to the main
thread to update V8 external memory accounting.

Because GetReadyState() has already reached kReadyStateHaveCurrentData
during the earlier CycleThreads() call, WaitForReadyStateHaveCurrentData
returns immediately without pumping media_thread_ or the main thread,
causing V8ExternalMemoryAccounterBase to intermittently still report 0.
Call CycleThreads() after WaitForReadyStateHaveCurrentData() to ensure
the memory usage report completes before asserting.

Test history:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fthird_party%2Fblink%2Frenderer%2Fcontroller%5C%3Ablink_unittests%21gtest%3A%3AWebMediaPlayerImplTest%23LoadPreloadMetadataSuspendNoVideoMemoryUsage

Support WebSocket over H3 variants in Chromium WPT runner

This change adopts https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63731
in WPT repo into chromium repo so that chromium also supports the opt-in
testing of WebSocket H3 variants wpt tests, and skip H3 variants by
default so that the h3 variants are skipped in default WPT runs. As h3
variant requires different test setup and will fail without those setup,
it is important to skip those tests when not opt-in to run them.

In later change, we will add test config to run all WebSocket variants
with EnableWebsocketsOverHttp3 feature enabled to verify that WebSocket
including WebSocket over h3 work as expected when the feature is
enabled.

[Glic] Launch GlicCookieSyncOnTokenChange on Android

Enable GlicCookieSyncOnTokenChange and GlicCookieSyncEarlyNoStartup by
default on Android, matching the launched configuration of the
GlicCookieSyncOnTokenChange study. Instead of syncing cookies into the
Glic partition every time the panel opens, sync happens when the primary
account's token changes and early when a Glic instance is created, which
keeps the sync off the panel-open path.

The feature flags are kept for now as a kill switch.

[Prompt API] Expose thinkingEffort in Blink

Expose `thinkingEffort` on `LanguageModel.create()`,
`LanguageModel.availability()`, per prompt options, and readonly
`session.thinkingEffort` behind the desktop experimental
`AIPromptAPIThinkingMode` runtime feature. Thought outputs remain hidden
in V1.

Sessions default to `"balanced"` sampling when `AIPromptAPIThinkingMode`
is enabled, and log a once per session DevTools console warning when
thinking runs with another sampling configuration. Also support
`thinkingEffort` in `EchoAI` for WPT coverage.

Restoring a tab after TabUtils.pauseMedia() previously called
WebContents.setAudioMuted(false) unconditionally, overriding the site's
sound content setting.

unmuting, and use it across the Android tab restore call sites.

[SafetyFRE] Resume the FRE from the last page after a relaunch

When Chrome is backgrounded during the FRE and reopened from the
launcher, the FRE restarts from the first page to show after the welcome
page. This is because a new FirstRunActivity is created without the
saved instance state/bundle, and the previous one is finished. In the
FRE progress, only skipping the welcome page is persisted, while the
rest lives in the saved instance state.

With this CL, the FRE resumes from the page the user last reached when
the Safety FRE promo is enabled, both when it is relaunched and when it
is recreated (e.g. theme changes). The Safety promo carousel resumes on
the Safety promo overview.

Demo http://shortn/_ezI8gOaNAM

In the follow-up CL, we will resume the carousel on the card the user
left off.

android: Remove extra quotes in date +%Z command in avd.py

DeviceUtils.RunShellCommand single-quotes each argument when passed a
sequence, so ['date', '+"%Z"'] executes `date '+"%Z"'` on the device and
returns '"UTC"' with literal double quotes. As a result, `timezone != 'UTC'`
in _EnsureSystemSettings was always True even when the emulator timezone
was already UTC.

Pass '+%Z' without embedded double quotes so the check works as intended.

d6a41cdb4f3ec53e1052f52a7d2d62b1849b755e [ diff ] 
[Spare RPH] Restore memory pressure gating of spare creation

Before this CL, when kStatefulMemoryPressure was enabled (the default on
Windows, macOS, and Linux since https://crrev.com/c/8415568) and
kKillSpareRenderOnMemoryPressure was disabled (the default everywhere),
memory pressure no longer prevented creating spare renderers.

https://crrev.com/c/8313508 routed the stateful creation gates in
WarmupSpare() and ShouldCreateExtraSpare() through
GetTargetSpareRPHCount(), which returns the full baseline count whenever
kKillSpareRenderOnMemoryPressure is disabled. Because creation used to
be gated independently of killing existing spares, reusing that target
allowed new spares to be launched under moderate and critical pressure.
Bots did not catch this because fieldtrial_testing_config.json enables
KillSpareRenderOnMemoryPressure.

This CL introduces ShouldScaleSparesWithMemoryLimit() so the granular
GetTargetSpareRPHCount() path is used only when stateful memory pressure
and kKillSpareRenderOnMemoryPressure are both enabled. Otherwise, spare
creation and limit updates fall back to the discrete memory_limit()
threshold checks: blocking the first spare at or below
GetMemoryLimitThreshold(), and blocking extra spares below
NoPressureThreshold(). Trimming of existing spares in OnReleaseMemory()
is unchanged.

[TabSwitcher] Share the default grid card size across cards

Grid cards now reuse the tab switcher's default card size instead of
each getting their own copy.

android.util.Size is immutable, so copying it gives every card a new
object that holds the same value. This happens for each card built and
for every card on each resize. The equals check before the first set was
also dead: the card model is always newly built there, so the size was
never already set.

No behavior change. The view binder only reads the width and height, and
a resize still sets a new size on every card.

Add separator rendering to tab group header

A collapsed tab group's header now paints the trailing separator that
its hidden tabs can't. In the legacy tab strip TabGroupHeader paints it;
in the unified tab strip UnpinnedTabContainerView paints it for each
TabGroupView and repaints it when the group's state or the following
slot changes. Tabs no longer paint a leading separator after a collapsed
group. The separator is hidden while the group collapses, in focus mode
and while dragging.

3a401384d0c16e148c2c771b579fbf0f788034c6 [ diff ] 
Support Document Policy in dedicated module workers

JS Self-Profiling in dedicated workers requires both the Profiler API
and a Document Policy that permits js-profiling. Earlier changes enabled
Document Policy for network dedicated workers
(https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7236250) and
added Document Policy inheritance for local-scheme dedicated workers
(https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/7857031).

Network module workers still initialized with an empty response Document
Policy bundle, so their script response could not enable profiling. This
CL closes that remaining gap, completing the Document Policy plumbing
needed for profiling in classic and module dedicated workers loaded from
network, blob and data URLs.

Parse the top-level module response's Document-Policy headers before
initializing a dedicated worker. Share response-header parsing with
classic workers, preserving local-scheme inheritance and preventing
imported module responses from changing the worker's policy.

Make the available Document Policy feature cache thread-local because
module response headers are parsed on worker threads. Check profiler
cleanup against the group's owning thread rather than requiring the main
thread, allowing worker shutdown and GC cleanup.

Remove browser test and CONTENT_EXPORT

[Android] Compute raw offset in ContentUiEventHandler mouse events

Previously, ContentUiEventHandler::SendMouseEvent() and
SendMouseWheelEvent() hardcoded raw_offset_x/y_pixels to 0, causing
mousedown, mouseup, and wheel events to carry view-local coordinates in
PositionInScreen() while EventForwarder::OnMouseEvent() carries true
screen coordinates. With DragThresholdRequiresMouseMovement enabled, any
ACTION_MOVE (including a 0px stationary move) between mousedown and
mouseup saw a screen-coordinate jump equal to the WebContents origin
offset, triggering a spurious dragstart and dropping clicks on draggable
links.

Compute raw_offset_x/y_pixels from MotionEvent.getRawX/Y() minus the
pointer's x/y pixels in both SendMouseEvent() and SendMouseWheelEvent(),
matching EventForwarder::OnMouseEvent().

[WebUI Toolbar] Fix reload button long-click behavior.

The reload button uses PressHandler, which distinguishes long presses/
drags, and short presses. The reload button does want different behavior
between the two, but only when devtools are open. When devtools is
closed, it doesn't want to distinguish the two.

This couldn't easily be done with PressHandler's API, because long
presses / drags are expected to open a menu, and so activate while the
mouse is down, while short presses activate on mouse up. So when
devtools is closed, we want to send short press events on mouse up, no
long press events, and not treat a press+drag as a long press.

This CL makes PressHandler take in an optional callback that can
dynamically enable/disable long press handling. The advantage of this is
it makes long press handling depend on state at the moment of long
press, instead of relying on a constant, and makes that pattern clear in
PressHandler.

We could instead set a bool on PressHandler whenever ability to show a
context menu changes, which would be a perfectly acceptable solution,
though the current code would treat that as, at least in part, depending
on context menu support at the point of mouse down.

[ModalDialog] Keep the close button at the end when there's no title

The title is the only weighted view in the title row. When a dialog
shows the close button but no title, ModalDialogView set the title to
GONE, so the close button moved to the start of the row. Keep the empty
title INVISIBLE whenever the row is shown, so it still fills the row
and the views after it, like the close button, stay at the end.

Only title rows shown without a title change. Shipped dialogs don't hit
this in practice: only Adaptive UI uses the close button, no feature
uses Adaptive UI yet, and dialogs with a title icon or end icon set a
title.

Introduce WebLocalFrameMetricsObserver for frame metrics notifications

This introduces blink::WebLocalFrameMetricsObserver as a dedicated
observer interface for frame metrics events, including subresource
loading, feature usage, user interactions, CPU timings, and layout
shifts.

MetricsRenderFrameObserver is updated to implement the new observer
interface. In addition, DidObserveSubresourceLoad and
DidObserveNewFeatureUsage are migrated from RenderFrameObserver and
WebLocalFrameClient to WebLocalFrameMetricsObserver, allowing the
removal of corresponding callback-based wiring in RenderFrame.

[soft navs] Add pre-navigation event timestamp browser test

Add SoftNavigationPreNavigationInputTest.PreNavigationEventTimestamp to
reproduce crbug.com/585428860 end-to-end in browser_tests without using
a synthetic or unadvanced test clock.

The test records a real monotonic timestamp via ui::EventTimeForNow()
before navigating away from a page with a beforeunload listener (which
ensures navigation_start advances after the timestamp via the browser ->
renderer -> browser round-trip), verifies the timestamp passes
ui::ValidateEventTimeClock() untouched (within its 60-second window),
and forwards a real click stamped with that timestamp after the new
document is ready (with --allow-pre-commit-input explicitly removed). It
then verifies the renderer remains live, a subsequent normal soft
navigation succeeds, renderer UMA records kInvalidTimeOrigin (16) and
kSoftNavigationDetected (0), and UKM records only the valid second soft
navigation with SoftNavigationCount == 1.

Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter=*PreNavigationEventTimestamp

Close open Views menu before running browser commands on macOS

On macOS, a browser shortcut pressed while the app menu's search field
has focus runs its command and leaves the menu open. Cmd+T opens a tab
underneath the menu. Cmd+F opens and focuses the find bar while the
menu stays up.

MenuController normally cancels an open menu on any Ctrl, Alt or Cmd
key press before the key reaches the browser window. It skips that
check while a menu textfield has focus, so that text-editing and system
shortcuts do not close the menu. Browser shortcuts then reach the
window's command handler with the menu still open.

Cancel any Views menu owned by the browser window in
BrowserNativeWidgetMac::ExecuteCommand, once WillExecuteCommand confirms
the command will run. The cancel sits there rather than in a key list
in MenuController because only keys that have already resolved to a
browser command reach ExecuteCommand. Editing shortcuts are consumed
earlier, by the textfield or by the Edit menu's own actions.

Replace the stale TODO in MenuController::OnWillDispatchKeyEvent with a
comment saying where browser commands cancel the menu. Add four macOS
tests to AppMenuSearchInteractiveTest.

Testing. The Mac-only code was written on Linux and first compiled on
the Mac trybots, which built patchsets 1 and 2. The results below are
from those patchsets, on mac-rel, before the rebase:
- Patchset 1, tests without the fix: the baseline test (field not
  focused, Cmd+T closes the menu) and the editing-shortcuts test (Cmd+A
  and Cmd+C keep the menu open) passed, 1 run each. The Cmd+T and Cmd+F
  tests with the field focused failed all 4 runs each. They timed out
  waiting for the menu to close, after the second tab had opened or the
  find bar had taken focus. All patchset 1 runs were on VMs with no
  display attached.
- Patchset 2, with the fix: each of the four tests passed 21 of 21
  runs, 1 on a physical Mac and 20 on a VM. The CQ dry run passed.

Patchset 4 rebases onto main, where crrev.com/c/8793503 had added tests
next to these in the same file. The lines this CL adds are unchanged.
The rebased code has not run on Mac yet; the patchset 4 dry run is the
check.

Not covered by any test or manual run:
- Two further symptoms predicted from the code: the find bar not
  accepting typing, and Cmd+N opening the new window behind the current
  one. Without the fix the Cmd+F test stops before its typing step, and
  no test presses Cmd+N.
- The emoji picker (Ctrl+Cmd+Space), dictation and input-source
  switching keeping the menu open. That they never resolve to a browser
  command rests on how AppKit dispatches them.
- The two failing tests on a physical Mac without the fix.
- The change tried by hand on a Mac.

[iOS][Omnibox] Measure multiline height with TextKit 1 layout manager

OmniboxContainerView previously measured user text height with
boundingRectWithSize: (TextKit 2), while its text view uses TextKit 1
(NSLayoutManager) for last-line clipping. Under locales such as de_DE,
TextKit 2 can break compound or dot-separated words into fewer lines
than TextKit 1 even with hyphenation disabled. Setting
maximumNumberOfLines to that smaller line count then clipped the wrapped
last line, hid the caret, and left the container stuck at a shorter
height.

Fix the layout mismatch and related multiline sizing edge cases:
- Measure user text with a reusable offscreen TextKit 1 stack configured
  to match the text view so line counts agree with its layout manager.
- Only cap maximumNumberOfLines when trailing non-user text (pre-edit,
  inline autocomplete, or additional text) needs clipping, and track the
  computed user-text line count separately for numberOfLines.
- Trigger layout whenever the ideal text height changes so scrollEnabled
  updates even after the clamped height constraint reaches its max.
- Coalesce text storage attribute updates during last-line clipping and
  add unit tests covering multiline expansion, clipping, and scrolling.

[Mac] Defer bookmark menu elision and favicons until interactive open

AppKit's accessibility / -[NSMenu _simulateOpening:] traversal invokes
menuNeedsUpdate:, menuWillOpen:, and menuDidClose: across every folder
submenu without posting NSMenuDidBeginTrackingNotification, and
OnProfileWillBeDestroyed() rebuilds the entire bookmark menu tree
recursively. Even when eliding each title once, HarfBuzz shaping and
async favicon requests across hundreds of thousands of bookmarks can
still block CrBrowserMain for ~24s (and ~20s on profile teardown).

Under kBookmarkMenuOptimizations, BookmarkMenuBridge now populates menu
items at menuNeedsUpdate: and OnProfileWillBeDestroyed() time with their
raw title and the cached default favicon, retaining submenu delegates
without starting favicon loads (and formatting tooltips eagerly only on
profile teardown while nodes still exist). BookmarkMenuCocoaController
observes NSMenuDidBeginTrackingNotification and
NSMenuDidEndTrackingNotification on the menu bar and invokes
BookmarkMenuBridge::OnMenuWillOpen() inside menuWillOpen: only during an
active menu-tracking session—idempotently eliding each item's title in
place (including after OnProfileWillBeDestroyed()) and setting tooltips
and favicons when the profile is alive. On an Apple Silicon macOS VM,
this cuts a 210K-bookmark non-interactive traversal from ~23s to <1s and
profile teardown from ~19s to ~1s (with ~25-40ms to interactively open a
100-item folder either before or after teardown).

Note: macOS Help-menu search (Cmd+Shift+?) opens the Help menu inside an
active menu-tracking session before walking menus, so it still finalizes
items eagerly.

[ui] Wait for initial tab load in RecentTabsSubMenuModelTest::AddBrowser

RecentTabsSubMenuModelTest::AddBrowser() opened a new window with
ui_test_utils::BROWSER_TEST_WAIT_FOR_BROWSER without waiting for the
initial tab's navigation to finish loading. In
RecentlyClosedWindowWithSplit and
RecentlyClosedWindowWithSplitAndRegularTabs, closing the new window
before Tab 0 ("about:blank?0") committed caused TabRestoreService to
omit Tab 0 from the restored window submenu.

Observe the new WebContents with content::TestNavigationObserver in
AddBrowser() so the initial tab finishes loading (including error-page
commits for synthetic URLs like "http://wnd1/tab0") before callers
manipulate splits or close the window.

Test history:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/test/chromium/%3A%2F%2Fchrome%2Ftest%5C%3Abrowser_tests%21gtest%3A%3ARecentTabsSubMenuModelTest%23RecentlyClosedWindowWithSplit

[WebView] Add a referrer parameter to navigate()

WebView#loadUrl uses a Referer header passed in additionalHttpHeaders as
the navigation's referrer, but the navigate API drops it, so apps that
use navigate() have no way to set the referrer. Rather than
special-casing the Referer header like loadUrl, add an explicit referrer
to the navigation parameters.

This is strictly additive: navigate() behaves the same unless an app
sets a referrer. A Referer header passed to navigate() is still ignored.

🌺 Revert "[Android] Prevent spurious long-presses in ForgivingClickAction"

This reverts commit cc58a78831f2519cfac086b069f2103e36518ed9.
Culprit: cc58a78831f2 - "[Android] Prevent spurious long-presses in ForgivingClickAction" (refs/heads/main@{#1749294}, https://crrev.com/c/8808956)

Reason for revert: consistently fails
android-desktop-17-arm64-rel-hylia-tests (and 2 other builders).

Mechanism: CL 8808956 replaced Tap.SINGLE in ForgivingClickAction with
ATOMIC_SINGLE_TAP, which omits Tap.SINGLE's inter-event quiescence wait
and post-ACTION_UP ~150ms settle delay. In
TabGridDialogTest#testCreateIncognitoGroupAndCloseAllTabsInDialogTwice_Bug354745444
(@EnableAnimations), Public Transit immediately clicks
@id/menu_select_tabs ~83ms after AppMenu PopupWindow creation while its
250ms @anim/menu_enter scale animation is still mid-flight, causing
InputDispatcher to dismiss PopupWindow as an outside touch and
TravelException to time out (8/8 failed across hylia #2420-#2421, brya
#3434-#3435, ruby #5988, plus 13 unrelated Try CLs).

TabGridDialogTest#testCreateIncognitoGroupAndCloseAllTabsInDialogTwice_Bug354745444
has failed in 2/2 recent builds of
android-desktop-17-arm64-rel-hylia-tests (and 5 failing verdicts across
3 builders overall), every attempt in every failing run. This is not
flake: it reproduces consistently, blocking the CQ for unrelated CLs
that touch this suite. The regression appears at
refs/heads/main@{#1749294}.

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/b/8664688850106839185

To run/deflake this test on CQ before relanding, add the following
footers to your CL description:
  Cq-Include-Trybots: luci.chrome.try:android-desktop-17-arm64-rel-hylia-tests
  Include-Ci-Only-Tests: chrome.android.desktop:android-desktop-17-arm64-rel-hylia-tests|chrome_public_test_apk

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

Original change's description:
> [Android] Prevent spurious long-presses in ForgivingClickAction
>
> ForgivingClickAction previously used Espresso's Tap.SINGLE [1], which
> waits for main-looper quiescence between injecting ACTION_DOWN and
> ACTION_UP [2]. On slow frames or active animations exceeding Android's
> long-press timeout (such as swangle_indirect Automotive builds), this
> turned single clicks into long-presses that opened context menus [3]
> instead of triggering click listeners.
>
> Dispatch forgiving single clicks via injectMotionEventSequence [4] with
> a 1ms DOWN-to-UP delta so both events are injected without mid-tap
> looper waits.
>
> [1]
> https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/8d4554af5ae3eacd242987e090bd083e2f767c35:base/test/android/javatests/src/org/chromium/base/test/util/ForgivingClickAction.java;l=51-68
> [2]
> https://github.com/android/android-test/blob/main/espresso/core/java/androidx/test/espresso/action/MotionEvents.java
> [3]
> https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/8d4554af5ae3eacd242987e090bd083e2f767c35:chrome/android/java/src/org/chromium/chrome/browser/toolbar/ToolbarManager.java;l=2849-2858
> [4]
> https://github.com/android/android-test/blob/main/espresso/core/java/androidx/test/espresso/base/UiControllerImpl.java
>
